subject: Skyline Therapeutics - Dedicated fleet burst mitigation and autoscale sizing
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@skyline-thera.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing and burst questions for pilot

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re lining up procurement for a Q3 pilot (drug-sim inference) and need to lock down Dedicated sizing and the burst/autoscale terms before legal will sign. A couple of specific asks: 

- Baseline GPU requirement: we expect a steady-state of ~18 GPU-equivalents during daytime batch windows, with stochastic spikes during model retrains and batch scoring.
- Burst behavior: we need short bursts (5-15 minutes) up to ~55 GPU-equivalents for heavy scoring episodes. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports transient bursts to that level and how throttling/eviction works?
- Autoscale policy: we want predictable cold-starts and an eviction policy that avoids dropping in-flight requests (or at least credits us appropriately).
- Can you share a sample SLA addendum that covers burst headroom and credit calculations?

If helpful, I attached our internal load profile (CSV). Looking to decide by end of week.

Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure
Skyline Therapeutics
[Attachment: skyline-load-profile.csv (csv, 48KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@skyline-thera.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing and burst questions for pilot

Priya —

Appreciate the load profile — useful. Short answers up front: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports transient burst to the level you described, and we can formalize an addendum for burst headroom, crediting, and eviction rules. Below is a pragmatic proposal that we recommend for pilot customers of your size. I’ve attached a worked sizing spreadsheet to walk through the numbers.

Key points: 
- Baseline reservation: 20 GPU-equivalents reserved. This covers your steady-state of 18 with a small buffer for background jobs.
- Shoulder/soft-burst policy: We can guarantee an additional 20 GPUs in the committed shoulder pool (warm VMs with fast spin-up) for bursts up to 30 minutes.
- Ephemeral burst tokens: For ephemeral high spikes, we offer a token-bucket style burst allowance that lets you exceed committed capacity up to +30 GPUs (total observed peak ~50) for short durations (typ. 10 minutes) before we start graceful throttling.
- Eviction & in-flight requests: We do not kill in-flight requests during a burst eviction window. Instead we (a) prioritize requests by route, (b) apply a throttling-rate to non-critical background jobs, and (c) for remaining excess requests we return 503 with a standard credit calculation equal to X% of hourly usage (see SLA addendum).

Operational suggestions for your pilot: 
- Canary ramp: start with 5 GPU-equivalents mirrored to production for one week, then 50% load for two days, then full cutover.
- Autoscale settings: min=20, target_util=0.7, scale_step=4 GPUs, scale_cooldown=90s. This keeps spin-ups smooth and avoids oscillation.
- Monitoring hooks: we'll enable per-route latency histograms and a cost-per-token dashboard so ops can see headroom consumption.

Attached: Skyline-Dedicated-Sizing.xlsx (worked example), Autoscale-Policy-EXAMPLE.md

Next steps: If this looks reasonable I’ll loop in Legal/Provisioning and draft an SLA addendum that captures burst credits, eviction policy, and canary windows.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: Skyline-Dedicated-Sizing.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Skyline burst policy inputs

LAUREN / BEN — quick internal thread before I respond to Priya’s follow-up. Copying the relevant excerpt below. Two items where I want ops judgment:

1) Headroom sizing: Priya asked about bursts to ~55 GPUs. Our plan above yields ~50 (20 reserved + 20 shoulder + 10 ephemeral tokens). Can we push ephemeral tokens to 30 for pilot maturity? Risk: additional preemptible spend and potential impact on other Dedicated customers if multiple clients spike concurrently.

2) Credit algorithm: Ben suggested a simple linear credit (minutes_over_x * reserved_rate * factor). Lauren, is that acceptable from an SLA/legal point of view? We should also cap total monthly credit to avoid open-ended liability.

Ben — please confirm runbook for eviction: do we gracefully queue or 503-first? Current recommended behavior: throttle background jobs first, queue critical short inference (<5s) up to 30s, then 503. Need to confirm whether queuing introduces headroom consumption while queued.

If we increase ephemeral tokens to +30 GPUs for the pilot, we should require an overage commit (e.g., pay-as-you-go for ephemeral minutes beyond a threshold) or a soft prepay.

-J

Jordan —

Thanks for the proposal. A few follow-ups from procurement/ops after reviewing the spreadsheet: 

- We can accept baseline reservation at 20 GPUs.
- We’re willing to pay for ephemeral minutes, but need hard limits so our finance team can forecast. Can you give an estimate of monthly ephemeral-minute consumption for our traffic profile and an overage price per GPU-minute?
- We want a guarantee that in-flight inference requests are not dropped for production routes (best-effort queueing for up to 30s is acceptable). For any 503 resulting from capacity exhaustion we’d prefer credits be applied against the monthly committed spend rather than settlement later.
- Final ask: include a clause that Redwood will provide a 2-week notice prior to reclaiming shoulder capacity for maintenance events that could affect burst headroom.

If you can incorporate these into the SLA addendum and send a DocuSign link, procurement can review and get this to legal.

Priya

Priya —

Great — thanks for the clear asks. I spoke with Ops and Legal this morning and here’s what we’ll put into the SLA addendum and pricing sheet: 

1) Ephemeral estimate & pricing: Based on your load profile we estimate ~4,200 GPU-minutes/month of ephemeral burst use if you hit 10 x 10-minute spikes per day. Overage price: $0.45 / GPU-minute for ephemeral bursts beyond the soft allotment. We’ll include a 15% bulk discount for the pilot term.

2) Queuing vs 503: Ops confirmed: production inference routes will be queued as first priority up to 30s. Background/low-priority work will be throttled/503’d first. If 503s occur on production routes we will automatically apply credits against that month’s committed spend equal to 2x the tokenized per-minute rate (formula will be spelled out). We will cap monthly credits at a contract-specific limit (suggested 10% of committed monthly spend).

3) Shoulder capacity notice: Redwood will provide a minimum 14-day notice prior to scheduled maintenance that could reduce shoulder capacity. Emergency maintenance will be communicated ASAP and will not exceed 6 hours except under force majeure.

4) Pilot constraint: For the pilot term we can increase ephemeral tokens to +30 GPUs (total observed peak ~60) provided Skyline agrees to a soft prepay of $5,000 that will be applied to any ephemeral overage. This mitigates risk for concurrent big spikes across customers.

Next actions I’ll take today: (a) prepare SLA addendum PDF with the above clauses, (b) update the sizing workbook with the 30-GPU ephemeral scenario, (c) send DocuSign for signature. Expect DocuSign link within 8 hours.

If that works, I’ll loop Legal and Provisioning once DocuSign is accepted and set a canary ramp schedule.

—Jordan
